items.name: Star rating
items.note: A rating from 1 to 5. Editable on a profile, read-only in lists and summaries. Used on Sedcard (Summary view).
rules: Editable: a radio group built from Bootstrap’s toggle buttons. The stars sit in a role="radiogroup" with aria-labelledby pointing at a visible label that says what is rated (for example “Text fluency”). Each star is a label.btn-check.btn-text.theme-secondary.btn-xs.btn-icon holding a radio with aria-label="n out of 5 stars".

Keyboard: Tab moves into the group and out to the next field. Right and Up add one star, Left and Down remove one (down to 0), Home sets 0 and End sets 5. The rating applies as it changes; no confirm step. Bootstrap’s focus ring shows on the focused star.

The current value shows as text after the stars (“4 stars”, “1 star”, “0 stars” when cleared; .fg-2) in an aria-live="polite" region, so screen readers announce each change. The radios keep their full names (“4 out of 5 stars”), so the scale is still announced. No tooltips on the stars: each radio already has its name, and tooltips only appear on mouse hover.

Never colour alone. Stars are --bs-fg-body, the body text colour (filmmakers.css sets it on .fm-rating), which passes 15:1 on white and grey.

Stars use btn-xs, a 24px target with no gap between stars. That meets the WCAG 2.2 AA minimum (2.5.8, 24 by 24px) and keeps the control compact for desktop, where most people use it. Do not go smaller. The star icons are the body text size (14px), as in production, in both the editable and the read-only rating.
When a rating is set, Clear rating follows the value (Tertiary, btn-text theme-secondary btn-sm); it hides when there is no rating.
In a form: help text and errors are linked with aria-describedby, an error sets aria-invalid="true", and a required rating sets aria-required="true" on the radiogroup (see Validation).

Read-only: the label, then star icons in a span.fg-3 (lighter than the editable stars, so a read-only rating does not look clickable; 5.2:1 or more on white and grey) with a title and a visually hidden “n out of 5 stars”. Two sizes: 14px (body text) by default, and 12px (.fs-xs on the whole rating, label included) in dense lists and tables. Keep it on one line (.text-nowrap).
Left aligned in its row, so nothing moves when the value text or Clear rating changes.

groups.title: Dialog
groups.intro: A short task or decision on top of the page.

items.name: Dialog
items.note: A short task or decision on top of the page: one decision, or a form of about six fields, finished in under 30 seconds. Bootstrap 6 Dialog, built on the native dialog element, which traps focus, closes on Esc and returns focus to the button that opened it.
rules: Use Bootstrap’s Dialog: a dialog.dialog opened by data-bs-toggle="dialog" and data-bs-target, closed by data-bs-dismiss="dialog". Label it with aria-labelledby pointing at the title.

Only for one short decision or a form of about six fields. Anything multi-step, needing its own URL, or a form that would need to scroll is a page. Dialogs never open dialogs, never stack and never appear unprompted.

Long read-only content (terms, a summary to review before confirming) may scroll inside the dialog: add .dialog-scrollable, Bootstrap’s default, so the header and footer stay fixed and the actions are always visible. Give the scrolling body tabindex="0" so keyboard users can scroll it.
Sizes: the default (500px) for most; .dialog-lg (800px) for a six-field form. No extra large or fullscreen dialogs: use a page.

Header: the title (h2.dialog-title.fs-md.fw-semibold) and Bootstrap’s close button (.btn-close, with aria-label="Close"). Footer: Cancel (Secondary) then the action, which names the outcome (“Save name”, never “OK” or “Submit”). All buttons btn-sm.
Focus: the first field gets focus when a form opens (autofocus); a confirmation focuses Cancel. Focus is trapped inside while open and returns to the button that opened the dialog when it closes.
Forms: data-bs-backdrop="static", so a click outside does not throw away what was typed. A dialog with an invalid field stays open and keeps the input (see Validation).

Confirming an irreversible action (Destructive actions): the title is a question naming the action and object (“Delete invoice INV-4021?”); the body says what is lost and that it cannot be undone; the action repeats the verb (“Delete invoice”, btn-solid theme-danger, with an icon so danger is not colour alone). Cancel and the action sit at opposite ends of the footer, and Cancel has focus when the dialog opens (autofocus). Esc cancels, never confirms.
Reversible actions never get a confirmation dialog: act at once and offer Undo in a Toast.

flags.text: Typed confirmation (“type DELETE to confirm”) for irreversible actions that affect other users or billed data: do we use it, and where? (Open in Destructive actions.)

Bootstrap 6 alpha keeps .dialog at visibility:hidden until its open transition starts, so the browser cannot move focus in on open. The Library focuses the autofocus control (or the first control) on shown.bs.dialog; production needs the same few lines until Bootstrap fixes it.

flags.text: To review: how filters inside More filters apply. Today each one applies on change, like the inline filters. Options: keep that; add an Apply filters button to the popover (a batch filter, which Carbon suggests when people set several filters at once or results are slow to load); or apply on close. The prototype opens Sort by with menu-end, which this Bootstrap build does not have. Use data-bs-placement="bottom-end".

rules: Order: search, inline filters (up to three), More filters, Clear filters, then Sort by at the far end.
Every filter is a Combobox reading label: value. Applied filters are weight 600, and More filters shows how many of its filters are applied.

The count row always shows, with the same range as the table footer, for example “5 of 12 profiles”, in 12px (fs-xs fw-semibold).

The bar fits filters to its width: each filter that no longer fits moves into More filters, then none are inline. When More filters and Sort by would overlap, both become icon buttons in one Button group (filter and sort icons, btn-outline theme-secondary as every Button group is, each with an accessible name and tooltip), and Clear filters moves to the bottom of the More filters popover. The icon buttons never change size and show no count; the applied count is in the filter button’s accessible name. On these widths the popover and menus fill the bar’s width.
The bar sits on the bg-1 surface at the top of the card that holds the list.

rules: One .card (article) per page. Content on the left, the Action gutter on the right (180px, --bs-bg-1, hairline on the inline-start edge). The old red-tinted gutter is gone: colour is for actions and states.
Image: 260px wide, 16:9, --bs-radius-5, hairline border, alt is the Project title. Leave it out when there is none; never a placeholder.
Title is an h2 at the section heading size (.fs-lg, weight 600). Description is body text, max 72ch.
Attachments are Chips that link to the file, one per file, with a file-type icon.
Details are a dl in two columns. Labels are .fg-3 at the same size and weight as values (as in the Definition list), with no colon. Show only fields that have a value.
Actions follow Row actions: btn-text theme-primary btn-xs, text and solid icon, in the fixed order Messages, Edit, then More.

More follows the Overflow menu: data-bs-placement="bottom-end" (this Bootstrap build has no .menu-end), 260–320px wide, descriptions wrap. The View as client items carry the client zone accent on the icon only and say “View as …” in text. Destructive items go last after a divider; Delete is theme-danger, and when disabled it has disabled, aria-disabled="true" and the reason as its visible description.

When the card is under 900px wide, the Action gutter becomes a bar along the bottom of the card, with the actions in a row at the end. The text drops under the image when the content is narrow, and the details wrap under the description.
User-written rich text (the description) keeps its <em> italics. This is an exception to the no-italics rule, which applies to product UI text only.

rules: One .card holding a .list-group.list-group-flush with role="list"; each row is a .list-group-item (role="listitem", padding 0). Every row in a list shares one grid-template-columns, so the columns line up.
Cells have 12px 16px padding. Stacked lines in a cell use an 8px gap; a title and its subtitle 2px.
The title is the row’s link, weight 600, followed by a .fg-3 meta suffix at the same size: (open), (Rank: #2). The whole row is not clickable. No italics for state.

Media: a fixed 132px, 16:9 thumbnail in every list that has media (as in production), --bs-radius-5, hairline border, alt is the title. When an item has no image, show the placeholder: a --bs-bg-2 box with a .fg-3 monitor icon (fa-display). Lists without media leave the column out.
Details sit on one line that wraps: the type as icon + weight 600 label in sentence case (not all-caps), the visibility as icon + text, then the stats.

Stats are icon + value. Each has a visually hidden label and a tooltip with the same name (e.g. Roles, Invitations), and is focusable so the tooltip opens on keyboard focus too. Icons inherit the text colour; success only for a state such as Selection status. Primary never tints icons or headings.
Short labels such as R: and A: are .fg-3, with the full words (Recording period, Airing) as visually hidden text.
Client visibility is an eye in the client zone colour when clients can see the content, and a .fg-3 eye-slash when they cannot, each with a tooltip and hidden text that say so.

The last column is the Action gutter (140–180px, one width per list), filling the row height, with Row actions stacked: Edit first, at most three visible, More last. Archive and Delete, or Remove, go in More with their explanation as a visible description. Delete is last, after a divider; a Remove that isn’t possible yet is disabled, with the reason.

When the card is under 900px wide, the row reflows: cells wrap onto new lines and the Action gutter becomes a bar along the bottom with the actions in a row at the end, like the Project card. No sideways scrolling.

flags.text: Changed from production: tooltips in the More menu became visible descriptions; Remove moved from the gutter into More (disabled with its reason); the all-caps type labels became sentence case; brand-coloured headings, stat icons and the orange client title became normal text, with the eye carrying client visibility; R:/A: labels became fg-3 with the full words hidden for screen readers; the ghost icon’s primary tint was dropped; FA5 icons became FA7 (fa-pencil-alt → fa-pencil, fa-th-large → fa-table-cells-large, fa-th-list → fa-table-list, fa-ticket-alt → fa-ticket).

Status markings: find every status marking these lists use in production, what each one means, and which ones stay. Known so far: the red outline on the current Selection row (episode.active), the orange title on a client-visible Selection (brand-client), the red highlighted count for new applications, the primary-tinted ghost icon for restricted profile visibility, the green Selection status check (color-booked), the eye / eye-slash for client visibility, and the planned / active row classes. Each kept marking needs a meaning, a colour role and a text equivalent.

New applications: production highlights the count in red (class highlight). Red means danger and primary must not mean new. This page shows the count as a weight 600 link with “3 new applications” in its tooltip. Decide how new items are marked.

Custom classes: Bootstrap has no class for the Action gutter or for rows that switch between a grid and wrapping, so this card and the Project card use three small classes in filmmakers.css (.fm-action-gutter, .fm-production-row, .fm-row-media). The Patterns overview says never invent a class name. Allow this short, documented list of fm- classes, or build without them?

items.note: One component for every row action group. Each action is a boolean prop (messages, edit, duplicate, viewAsApplicant, copyMove, unsubscribe, remove, more), so pages cannot drift. layout="stack" fills an Action gutter; layout="inline" sits in a table cell. rules: Every action is a Row action: btn-text theme-primary btn-xs, icon plus text label. Edit is a link (a) because it navigates; the rest are buttons.
Fixed order on every row: Messages, Edit, Duplicate, View as applicant, Copy/Move, then More. Turning an action off never reorders the rest.
At most three actions show. Each page chooses which three; the choice is the same on every row of that page. The rest go into More, which is always last and always opens a .menu.
Unsubscribe and Remove are never bare controls. They go last in More, after a divider, as menu-item theme-danger, and follow Destructive actions (undo if reversible, confirm if not).
More carries an accessible name with the row, e.g. “More actions for Season 14: Erste Runde”, so repeated triggers are distinguishable.
Stack has no gap between buttons; inline uses an 8px gap.
